hypothesis: Per the FwFM literature finding (field-weighted FM as a cheap FFM alternative), replace the FM's uniform "sum over all field-pair interactions" with per-field-pair scalar weights r_{i,j} (only F(F-1)/2=10 extra parameters for our 5 fields, initialized to 1.0 so it starts identical to plain FM) that let the model learn e.g. that the user×video interaction matters more than tab×duration — this is a targeted capacity increase within the same pairwise-interaction structure that BPR+FM already trains well, unlike the failed DeepFM MLP branch which added a structurally mismatched higher-order pathway.
reflection: Iter 12's web-research question specifically surfaced "field-weighted FM as cheap alternative to full field-awareness" (FwFM, Pan et al. WWW 2018) as an established, CPU-cheap way to get most of FFM's benefit without the O(F²k) embedding blowup — I have that finding in hand and should act on it now rather than spend another research call, since plain order-2 FM has plateaued across features/regularization/negative-sampling/capacity for 6 straight iterations and this is a genuinely untried mechanism (learned per-field-pair interaction weights) rather than a variant of anything already tested.
expected_effect: GAUC should move more than nDCG@5, since FwFM directly refines the pairwise interaction score that BPR trains and that GAUC's pairwise-correctness definition measures, whereas nDCG@5's top-5 ranking is a more indirect consequence of that same score.
